description: Phase 6bg gate — RETURNING clause on INSERT / UPDATE / DELETE. After the DML operation, project the affected rows as a result set.

program.sql: CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, v INTEGER);
INSERT INTO t (v) VALUES (10) RETURNING id;
CREATE TABLE t (a INTEGER, b INTEGER);
INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, 10) RETURNING *;
CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, v INTEGER);
INSERT INTO t (v) VALUES (10), (20), (30) RETURNING id, v ORDER BY id;
CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER, v INTEGER);
INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, 10), (2, 20);
UPDATE t SET v = v * 10 RETURNING id, v ORDER BY id;
CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER, v INTEGER);
INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, 10), (2, 20), (3, 30);
DELETE FROM t WHERE v >= 20 RETURNING id;
CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, v INTEGER);
INSERT INTO t (v) VALUES (5) RETURNING id, v * 2 AS doubled;
CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER, v INTEGER);
INSERT INTO t VALUES (1, 10), (2, 20), (3, 30);
UPDATE t SET v = 999 WHERE id = 2 RETURNING id, v;

cases.name: returning-no-rows
cases.description: DELETE matching zero rows with RETURNING returns empty set, not error.

program.sql: CREATE TABLE t (id INTEGER);
INSERT INTO t VALUES (1);
DELETE FROM t WHERE id = 99 RETURNING id;
